span.label: whether the firing patterns that gave place cells and grid cells their names are about physical space, or about any continuous task-relevant variable
span.quote: Our results therefore suggest that the well-known spatial patterns in the hippocampal/entorhinal circuit may be a consequence of the continuous nature of the relevant task variables (e.g., location), rather than a primacy of physical space for this network

span.label: whether the hippocampal and entorhinal circuit represents an arbitrary non-spatial continuous dimension with the same discrete firing fields it uses for location
span.quote: However, the hippocampal/entorhinal circuit is involved not only in spatial navigation, but in a variety of memory-guided behaviors 6 . The relationship between this general function and the specialized spatial activity patterns is unclear. A conceptual framework reconciling these views is that spatial representation is just one example of a more general mechanism for encoding continuous, task-relevant variables

span.label: the same neurons, including identified place cells and grid cells, tile a sound-frequency axis with discrete firing fields in a task containing no spatial dimension
span.quote: We tested this idea by recording hippocampal and entorhinal neurons in a task that required rats to use a joystick to manipulate sound along a continuous frequency axis. We found neural representation of the entire behavioral task, including activity that formed discrete firing fields at particular sound frequencies. Neurons involved in this representation overlapped with the known spatial cell types in the circuit like place cells and grid cells.

span.label: existence
span.quote: We found neural representation of the entire behavioral task, including activity that formed discrete firing fields at particular sound frequencies.

span.label: hippocampal-entorhinal coding of a non-spatial continuous dimension
span.quote: We tested this idea by recording hippocampal and entorhinal neurons in a task that required rats to use a joystick to manipulate sound along a continuous frequency axis.

span.label: electrophysiology
span.quote: We recorded 2208 units in the dorsal CA1 of 5 rats and 1164 units in the dorsal MEC of 9 rats ( Extended Data Fig. 2 ).

span.label: mechanisms
span.term: Spatial firing arises because location happens to be a continuous task-relevant variable, not because physical space is privileged for this circuit
span.quote: Our results therefore suggest that the well-known spatial patterns in the hippocampal/entorhinal circuit may be a consequence of the continuous nature of the relevant task variables (e.g., location), rather than a primacy of physical space for this network

span.label: mechanisms
span.term: Performing a task drives a sequence of firing fields that are elicited parametrically as behaviour progresses
span.quote: In this framework, task performance activates a sequence of neural activity, in which firing fields are elicited parametrically with progress through behavior.

span.label: mechanisms
span.term: Overlap between neighbouring fields encodes the order and adjacency of behavioural states, supporting episodic linking and planning
span.quote: Neighboring and partially overlapping fields therefore represent the order and adjacency of behavioral states.

span.label: traversal speed is randomised trial by trial so that sound frequency and elapsed time are uncoupled, which is what makes a frequency field distinguishable from a time field
span.quote: To uncouple frequency from the amount of elapsed time, we randomly varied, across trials, the “speed” of frequency traversal. Resulting trials varied in duration by up to a factor of 2, on average in the range of 5–10 s.

span.label: a model tested the strength of alignment of the neural activity to various task events, and each field was found to align best either to particular sound frequencies or to the press or the release of the joystick
span.quote: To quantify this frequency locking, we implemented a model that tested the strength of alignment of the neural activity to various task events ( Extended Data Fig. 7 ). Of the fields that occurred during sound presentation, more than half in both CA1 and MEC aligned best to particular sound frequencies, whereas the rest were more strongly time-locked either to the press or to the release of the joystick

span.label: the proposed general mechanism is that task performance activates a progression of firing fields, so that neighbouring and overlapping fields represent the order and adjacency of behavioural states
span.quote: However, our observations lead to an intriguing conjecture that in more complex tasks (e.g. those containing memory-guided decision points), the hippocampal/entorhinal system might similarly represent arbitrary behavioral states. In this framework, task performance activates a sequence of neural activity, in which firing fields are elicited parametrically with progress through behavior. Neighboring and partially overlapping fields therefore represent the order and adjacency of behavioral states.

span.label: and the absence of field broadening across the trial is attributed to an informative sensory variable being continuously available, unlike in a delay task where the code can drift
span.quote: Note that fields in the SMT did not progressively broaden during the delay period, as they typically do in time cells; this may be due to the fact that an informative sensory variable (sound frequency) was always available to the animal, preventing a drift in the neural code.

span.label: Too few fields per grid cell in the sound task to test whether its firing corresponds to a one-dimensional slice through a hexagonal grid lattice.
span.quote: One possibility is that the SMT firing patterns corresponded to 1-dimensional slices through a hexagonal lattice 25 ; however, the small number of fields produced by grid cells in the SMT (typically 0–3) precluded this analysis.

span.label: The task itself did not require the animals to represent the whole acoustic dimension, so the functional necessity of the representation is not established.
span.quote: In the SMT, rats did not actually need to represent the structure of the entire acoustic space.

span.quote: The three clusters in were not perfectly separated; in fact, some firing fields had significantly non-zero regression coefficients for more than one task parameter: 14% in CA1 and 21% in MEC (p<0.01, bootstrap analysis).

span.quote: In the SMT, rats did not actually need to represent the structure of the entire acoustic space. They could, in fact, respond to a particular sound frequency – a strategy also sufficient in operant tasks that are known to be hippocampus-independent

span.quote: We detected fewer grid cells in the smaller environment that we used than in the larger one. This is consistent with previous studies (e.g. 35 ) and might potentially be due to an insufficient number of fields for reliable grid detection or to boundary influences on the firing of grid cells 36 , 37 . We therefore verified all comparisons of grid and non-grid cells on the subset of cells that were recorded in the larger environment.

span.label: a tightening of firing fields in the vicinity of joystick presses and releases may be due to a higher density of available sensory cues, or alternatively may result from the stronger salience of these events
span.quote: Fields were concentrated near the press and the release of the joystick and were narrower during these time. (e–h) Statistics in MEC for 943 fields in 1164 cells, plotted as in (a–d). MEC tended to have more fields/cell than CA1, but otherwise had similar statistics. A tightening of firing fields in the vicinity of joystick presses and releases may be due to a higher density of available sensory cues during these events. Alternatively, field tightening may result from the stronger salience of these events compared to the rest of the task.

span.label: and a head-direction confound had to be excluded by a separate analysis, since head direction cells overlap the modulated population
span.quote: Head direction (HD) cells overlap with SMT-modulated neurons, but do not fully account for firing rate modulations in the SMT. This analysis was performed to account for the possibility that some SMT firing was due to subtle changes in HD in the nosepoke or between the nosepoke and the lick-tube.

Thus, SMT-modulated and spatially selective neurons were not distinct subclasses of the circuit, but represented a shared use of the same neural population between tasks.

Animals deflected a joystick to activate a pure tone produced by a sound speaker. They continued deflecting in order to increase frequency along a perceptually uniform logarithmic axis 22 . Rewards were obtained by releasing the joystick within a fixed target frequency range.

span.label: SMT → linear track
span.note: AN ANALOGY, BOUNDED BY ITS AUTHORS: the sound-manipulation task evolves along a continuous axis (sound frequency) and is therefore ANALOGOUS to spatial navigation on a linear track, SHARING SOME KEY FEATURES of neural representation - discrete firing fields tiling the task, multiple fields in MEC cells, clustering at salient features, and context-dependence. `Some key features` is the authors' own bound and it is the part an equivalence edge deletes.
span.quote: Because the SMT evolves along a continuous axis (sound frequency), it is analogous to spatial navigation on a linear track. Our results show that it shares some key features of neural representation with this task. Just like location, the non-spatial dimension is represented in the hippocampal/entorhinal system by discrete firing fields that continuously tile the entire behavioral task. Several other properties are shared, including a tendency of MEC cells to produce multiple fields 2 , a clustering and tightening of fields at salient features of the task 26 , 27 , and a dependence of the firing on behavioral context

span.label: MEMBERSHIP OF A NAMED CLASS BARELY PREDICTS THE SAME CELL IN ANOTHER TASK: the amount of task modulation had a very weak correlation with placeness and gridness, r2 about 0.005, which is read as nearly independent activity patterns
span.quote: Both place cells and grid cells were somewhat less likely to be SMT-modulated than other cells in their respective brain regions (34.7% of the 623 CA1 non-place cells and 46.5% of the 776 MEC non-grid cells; p<0.001 and p<0.02, χ 2 test, respectively). However, the amount of SMT modulation across neurons had a very weak correlation to measures of both “placeness” and “gridness” 23 (r 2 =0.0054 and r 2 =0.0053, respectively; Fig. 4c,d ), suggesting nearly independent activity patterns in the two tasks.

span.label: THE DEFINITION OF THE TYPE IS A THRESHOLD ON THIS DATASET'S OWN SHUFFLES: grid cells are cells whose grid score exceeds the 95th percentile of the shuffled samples, which in this dataset was 0.46
span.quote: To detect grid cells, we computed the grid score 23 , using the exact procedure described in 31 . The grid score measured the spatial correlation of a cell’s rate map to its own rotation at 60° and 120° and compared it to the correlation at 30°, 90°, and 150° rotations. Firing rate maps with symmetry that was specific to 60° had high grid scores. We measured the 95 th percentile of the grid scored across all shuffled samples from all the MEC cells we recorded. In our dataset, this value was 0.46. Cells whose grid score exceeded this value were considered grid cells.

span.label: and place cells are cells whose spatial information exceeds 99% of their own shuffled values, so both categories are defined relative to the recording rather than absolutely
span.quote: To detect place cells, we calculated “spatial information” 34 – the mutual information rate between spikes and location – using the same formula as above ( Eqn. 2 ), but using the 1600 spatial bins instead of time bins. Place cells were defined as cells for which the information rate exceeded 99% of the values for the shuffled samples.

span.label: AND THE COUNT OF A CELL TYPE DEPENDS ON THE ARENA: fewer grid cells were detected in the smaller environment than the larger one, so every grid comparison was re-verified on the subset recorded in the larger environment
span.quote: We detected fewer grid cells in the smaller environment that we used than in the larger one. This is consistent with previous studies (e.g. 35 ) and might potentially be due to an insufficient number of fields for reliable grid detection or to boundary influences on the firing of grid cells 36 , 37 . We therefore verified all comparisons of grid and non-grid cells on the subset of cells that were recorded in the larger environment.

span.label: AN EXCLUSION CRITERION THAT DOES NOT EXIST OUTSIDE THE TASK IT WAS BUILT FOR: sharp-wave ripples are normally removed by rejecting low-velocity time points, and with no velocity in this task they had to be detected directly in the field potential
span.quote: In CA1, some of the spikes were produced during sharp-wave ripple events (SWR). During spatial navigation experiments, such events are typically excluded from firing rate maps by rejecting low-velocity time points. In the SMT, we instead excluded SWRs by directly detecting them in the local field potential

span.label: with the negative disclosure attached: excluding those spikes did not qualitatively change any result, it only raised the in-field to background ratio
span.quote: Exclusion of these spikes did not qualitatively change any of our results, but tended to increase the ratio of the in-field firing rates to the background.

span.label: THETA DID NOT TRACK SPEED HERE, UNLIKE IN NAVIGATION, which is read as the navigation relationship being dependent on locomotion-related signals
span.quote: Frequency of theta oscillations quantified across trials that had different average “speeds” of sound frequency traversal in the SMT. Symbols: mean ± s.e.m. across rats. Red line: linear regression fit; the slope of the fit was not significantly different from 0 (p = 0.70). Unlike in spatial navigation, theta frequency did not correlate to speed; this may imply that the relationship between theta and speed during navigation is dependent on locomotion-related signals.

span.label: THE CONTROL IS DECOMPOSED RATHER THAN RUN ONCE: passive playback alone engaged almost no cells, passive playback with a reward engaged a fifth of them with wider fields, so context matters and agency is not strictly required
span.quote: Firing fields in this passive playback+reward task were also wider than in the SMT (2.49±0.29 s and 1.16±0.05 s; N=1252 and 44 fields, respectively; p<0.001, Wilcoxon rank-sum test; Fig. 3e ). Thus, behavioral context affected the fraction of neurons activated and their temporal precision. However, the coupling between actions and sounds (i.e. agency) was not strictly required to engage hippocampal activity.

span.quote: Grid cells occur in discrete “modules” with distinct spacings and widths of the firing fields 24 . SMT-modulated cells included grid cells from all modules detectable in our data ( Fig. 4b ). The distributions of field widths were indeed different between modules 1 and 2/3 (0.78±0.02 s and 1.36±0.05 s, respectively; N=48 and 51 cells, median±s.e.m.; p<0.01, Wilcoxon rank-sum test; Fig. 4e ). Thus, grid cells with wider fields in the spatial environment tended also to have wider fields in the SMT, suggesting shared neural mechanisms.
